links.comparator_used: Usual care (control period before each clinic's stepped-wedge rollout), with no ML-risk-targeted prompts
links.outcome: Serious illness conversation (SIC) rate at encounters with patients flagged high-risk (10% or higher predicted 6-month mortality)
links.effect: High-risk encounters: unadjusted SIC rate 3.4% (59/1754) in the control period vs 13.5% (510/3765) in the intervention period; aOR 2.62 (95% CI 1.84-3.72). All encounters: aOR 2.09 (1.53-2.87). Non-high-risk encounters: aOR 2.07 (1.52-2.82).
links.quote: The intervention was associated with significant increases in SICs among all patient encounters (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53–2.87]; P < .001), those with high-risk patients (aOR, 2.62 [95% CI, 1.84–3.72]; P < .001), and those with non–high-risk patients (aOR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.52–2.82]; P < .001).

links.comparator_used: Usual care (control period before rollout); the trial did not test the risk prediction alone
links.outcome: Sustained SIC rate and end-of-life systemic therapy over 40 weeks
links.effect: SIC rates for all encounters rose from 1.3% (158/12 356) to 4.4% (1262/28 665), about 4 times baseline after 6 months. End-of-life systemic therapy fell from 10.4% (24/231) to 7.5% (72/957); aOR 0.25 (95% CI 0.11-0.57). No effect on inpatient death, ICU use, hospice enrollment or hospice length of stay.
links.quote: First, our intervention led to a sustained increase in SICs, and rates remained nearly 4 times above baseline after 6 months.

design_hint: ML-triggered clinician nudges (peer comparison emails, high-risk lists, opt-out text prompts)
